statement: For a multiplicative-type group G with character sheaf M, a principal discrete/profinite π-cover trivializing M with continuous module M₀, and a constant coefficient ring Λ acting on O_S, the co-Lie complex is f*(M₀⊗ᴸ_ZΛ)⊗ᴸ_ΛO_S. The last tensor is ordinary if Λ is a field. This continues the formula ℓ_G≃M⊗ᴸ_ZO_S on cote 8:78.

statement: H⁰(ℓ_G)=M⊗_ZO_S and H⁻¹(ℓ_G)=Tor¹_Z(M,O_S); in characteristic p these are (M/pM)⊗FpO_S and M[p]⊗FpO_S. For a locally free finite Λ=Z/n module sheaf M, the two terms are E=M⊗ΛO_S and the Postnikov class lies in Ext²(E,E)=H²(S,End E), induced from H²(S,End M).

statement: The earlier run proposes comparing the local-system-induced Ext² class here with the obstruction/deformation comparison in cote 100:37.

his_words: sans doute pas nulle si M₀ de rang d≥2
statement: For n=p prime, the obstruction to lifting the universal rank-d representation of GL_d(Fp) to a free Z/p²-module vanishes for d≤1; the page expects nonvanishing for every d≥2. It attributes the interpretation as a lifting obstruction to Illusie.
reconstruction: The universal obstruction is the extension class of GL_d(Z/p²)→GL_d(Fp) with conjugation coefficients End(Fp^d). The all-d≥2 assertion has small exceptions; the earlier run’s proposed test is retained as its own idea.

statement: For the universal covering used to trivialize M, the map H²(Bπ,End M₀)→H²(S,End M) is asserted injective, so a nonzero universal obstruction remains nonzero on S.
reconstruction: The valid form uses the Cartan–Leray low-degree sequence and H¹(S′,constant End M₀)=0; the dash in H²(Bπ,−) is not interpreted as every possible sheaf. For finite locally constant coefficients the universal étale cover gives this vanishing in the appropriate pro-cover formulation.

statement: The title and intervening stationery/Italian vocabulary sheets establish the internal organization of the first cote 9 group. They provide no additional mathematical theorem and no reliable new date.

statement: For a p-divisible group G over a perfect field of characteristic p, its reduced Dieudonné module has dimension height(G), a Hodge exact sequence with ω_G and t_G*, and duality exchanging F and V. Connectedness corresponds to nilpotence of the appropriate reduced F, and connectedness of G* to nilpotence of V, in the contravariant convention.
reconstruction: Perfectness and a fixed covariant/contravariant convention are required. The formulas involving p-power derivations and the ambiguous H^(2|1)(G,Ga) are preserved as an unfinished identification. Pro’s “G sans tore” needs a star if it is meant to restate connectedness of the dual.
check_reason: Codex reads G* sans tore where Pro reads G sans tore. The multiplicative p-divisible group μ_p∞ separates these statements. The pairing and nilpotence facts are established, but the ambiguous cohomological superscript is not repaired.

statement: The pages construct coefficient-of-1 functionals on truncated Dieudonné rings, propose a dualizing bimodule/direct-limit model, and compare duals Hom_W(M,W) with a twisted ring-action dual. They warn that two W-actions differ and write adjointness identities for F,V.
reconstruction: This package does not determine a consistent truncation index without checking W_n versus F^(n+1),V^(n+1). A displayed V-dual action precomposed with F contradicts the later V_g formula and FV=p. The full bimodule theorem is not certified from this ambiguous presentation.
check_reason: The earlier notes correctly isolate the twists but miss the Pro/Codex cancellation discrepancy: Codex deletes the proposed finite-ring isomorphism on scan7. The coefficient calculation and the actual F/V-adjoint duality are separated from this undecided draft.

statement: A canceled sheet asks for a direct Gauss–Manin connection on Rf_*Ω and drafts a descent lemma: local degree-zero chain maps parametrized by a torsor differ by prescribed chain homotopies, and should yield a derived-category morphism functorial in the target and in torsor changes.
reconstruction: A rigorous descent statement needs coherent higher descent data or an explicit enhancement; the torsor relation alone is recorded, not upgraded to a theorem. The displayed composition has a possible type-order error.
check_reason: The entire sheet is canceled in both transcriptions. Its local lemma must not appear as a live proved construction. The general Gauss–Manin objective has a later direct construction, without certifying this exact canceled lemma.

statement: Over a complete henselian DVR with perfect residue field, a generic-fiber p-divisible group with a filtration whose factors acquire good reduction over a finite Galois extension is assigned a Grothendieck-group class of equivariant integral models of those factors. Uniqueness of the factor models is attributed to Tate.
reconstruction: The inserted unequal-characteristic restriction belongs to the invocation of Tate’s theorem. Independence of the chosen filtration and descent datum must still be justified; the page does not prove them.
check_reason: The notes correctly distinguish the extension theorem from the unproved K₀ construction. Equal characteristic cannot be silently included in the historically cited Tate theorem.

statement: After restriction to the special fiber and covariant Dieudonné realization, inertia acts W(k′)-linearly. Its trace is a central function on inertia, equivariant under the residual quotient acting by both conjugation and Witt-vector automorphisms; a direct-limit character independent of the good-reduction extension is asserted.
reconstruction: Distinguish G-semilinearity from I-linearity, and coefficient G/I-action from ordinary invariance. Additivity and enlargement compatibility are required for the asserted virtual character.
check_reason: The manuscript explicitly changes the coefficient action and passes among extensions. It asserts, but does not prove, the required independence.

statement: For potentially constant p-divisible groups, the p-regular inertia trace is compared with the Brauer character of M[p]. The attempted unrestricted Brauer-character comparison is immediately rejected using the multiplicative group/cyclotomic representation.
reconstruction: Take K=Qp, p>2: μ_p∞ has good reduction, hence trivial special-fiber inertia, while its mod-p cyclotomic representation has nontrivial prime-to-p inertia. This refutes the proposed equality of characters. It does not by itself supply two arbitrary groups with isomorphic M[p] and unequal characters.
check_reason: The withdrawal and its scope are on the page. The later assumption μp⊂K is a new restricted question, not a repair of the unrestricted assertion.

statement: With μp⊂K, the page asks whether potentially good elliptic curves with isomorphic mod-p Galois modules have equal p-regular inertia characters, with supersingular reduction singled out. A constant-torsion variant is followed by a margin read “faux par Tate”. For p≠2,3 the geometric special-fiber automorphism group is cyclic of order2,4,or6; inertia is a subgroup, so orders1 and3 are also possible.
reconstruction: The marginal denial has no unambiguous attachment or example. An independent p=5 counterexample is proved in proofs.md; it is not attributed to Tate. Its characters are those of finite potentially-good monodromy, equivalently ℓ-adic inertia for ℓ≠5, not literal full5-adic Tate-module inertia. The rank of an abelian variety’s full Dieudonné module is 2g, so the displayed general trace n=dim A needs checking against the later elliptic value2. Automorphism-group statements apply after passage to geometric special fiber and inertia, not arbitrary residue Galois action.
check_reason: The notes preserve the doubt but do not settle the leader of the Tate annotation. The broad dimension normalization and the distinction between inertia and the whole Galois group are material.

his_words: Cela implique sans doute que A₀ est ordinaire
statement: For the universal infinitesimal deformations of an abelian variety A₀ in characteristic p, seek a full k-stratification of H¹_dR functorial in A, compatible with base change and with F,V. Constancy of the geometric F,V-module type is suggested to force ordinarity.
reconstruction: This is stronger than merely having a Gauss–Manin connection. The claimed necessity of ordinarity depends on allowing all deformations and on the exact F,V-compatibility; the manuscript supplies neither a proof nor a precise universal obstruction.
check_reason: The opening is a question and the necessity is explicitly “sans doute”. The earlier run’s proposed ordinary-family calculation remains its own programme.

statement: Ordinarity splits the Hodge sequence by Im F. To show the desired stratification preserves Hodge, the argument first obtains equality after Frobenius pullback, warns that this need not descend over arbitrary nilpotent bases, then uses faithful flatness of Frobenius on the formally smooth universal deformation space and specializes back.
reconstruction: Equality of subbundles descends under faithfully flat base change. Over Fp[ε]/ε² it does not descend under Frobenius; an explicit pair of lines verifies the warning. Formal-smoothness/perfect-base hypotheses belong to the descent step.
check_reason: The continuation to scan18 closes the particular descent concern; scan17 must not be cited as a final gap without the next page.

his_words: il y en a déjà une
statement: For an ordinary abelian scheme, the Hodge and conjugate pieces split H¹_dR. The tangent bundles are scalar extensions of finite locally constant Fp-sheaves determined by unit Frobenius; hence they carry canonical full stratifications respecting those unit structures. Ordinary p-torsion has a connected/radicial factor and a finite étale quotient.
reconstruction: The discrete group is GL_g(Fp), interpreted as a constant finite group, not the positive-dimensional algebraic GL_g over k. The resulting stratification is not identified with the Gauss–Manin connection; its preserved Hodge filtration explains the manuscript’s warning about an uninformative classification principle.
check_reason: The note appropriately marks “à préciser”; the unit-Frobenius/local-system formulation supplies that precision. The factorization is kept relative to S, not replaced by a chosen splitting over a general base.

statement: The page shifts between étale Fp-sheaves and duals of A[p](k). Literal k-rational points do not recover the rank-g tangent space over every perfect field. A correct fiberwise statement uses geometric points with Galois descent, or the associated étale sheaf. The earlier run links this to Frobenius-stable de Rham augmentation in cote 4:6.
reconstruction: The counterexample E/F5:y²=x³−x has eight rational points, is ordinary, and has E[5](F5)=0. Thus this is a genuine mathematical alarm, not merely a preference for sheaf notation. The letter Φ versus calligraphic L remains a scan issue.
check_reason: Perfectness alone is insufficient for the displayed rational-point formula. Both link endpoints were read; their connection is through unit-Frobenius descent and dualization, not an unqualified equality of all cohomology objects.

statement: For an ordinary abelian scheme, the de Rham class of a relative Néron–Severi section lies in the middle factor of ∧²(H¹⁰⊕H⁰¹), and corresponds to the tangent map of its homomorphism λ:A→A*. The map is compared with the transpose of λ on étale p-torsion after scalar extension.
reconstruction: Retain the live direction t_A→t_A*. The canceled paragraph used the opposite direction through an alternating-form convention. Relative Chern-class and duality conventions must be fixed before identifying all signs.
check_reason: The earlier notes correctly distinguish canceled and live arrows. The compatibility is stated, rather than demonstrated, on this page.

statement: The determinant of the p-power tangent map t_A^(p)→t_A defines a section Ha_A of ω_A^(p−1), with ω_A=det(t_A)^∨. It is a unit exactly on the ordinary locus, so its set of zeros is the nonordinary locus.
reconstruction: The line dual is essential. Scheme-theoretic multiplicities and higher rank strata are proposed only by the earlier run, not claimed by the manuscript. The canceled meromorphic-extension route is replaced by the direct determinant construction.
check_reason: The notes correctly distinguish a zero set from a stratification with multiplicities, and flag the inconsistent L/ω and determinant-dual notation.

statement: The determinant of the Hodge exact sequence, together with top de Rham trace, produces a canonical isomorphism ω_A≃ω_A*. The author asserts compatibility with the ordinary unit-F structures and equality of their Hasse invariants, hence a determinant comparison on étale p-torsion.
reconstruction: The precise normalization of top exterior powers and the order of factors affect signs. The construction is on determinant lines; it does not yield an isomorphism of the full rank-g p-torsion representations.
check_reason: The page gives the line construction and asserts the compatibility; it does not prove the compatibility or a higher-rank isomorphism.

statement: Cartier duality interchanges the étale and multiplicative factors of an ordinary p-divisible group of an abelian scheme. Over a perfect field the group splits into these factors; over a general base their extension class must be included, and the author asks for it explicitly.
reconstruction: The general extension is described in Serre–Tate deformation theory by bilinear formal multiplicative parameters. The earlier note’s comparison to cote 100’s reconstruction data is only structural: that source concerns gluing by local data, not the same functor.
check_reason: The page distinguishes perfect-base reconstruction from the unresolved general extension. Both cote 100 link endpoints were read and remain outside the SA15 claims census.

statement: For an ordinary abelian variety A over a perfect field, construct a polarization-independent isomorphism α_A:det T_p(A)_et→det T_p(A*)_et by dividing det T_p(λ)_et by the positive integer √deg λ. The manuscript reduces independence to positive Rosati-symmetric quasi-endomorphisms, supplies a real-square-root sign argument on scan 27, and checks the integral lattice by the self-dual polarization kernel on scan 28.
reconstruction: The page’s earlier uncertainty about the sign is resolved locally by its later argument; it is not a surviving conjecture. Rationality of the determinant polynomial follows by interpolation, not by the canceled false equality Zp[T]∩Q[T]=Z[T]. Integral normalization requires the ordinary connected/étale split and Cartier self-duality of ker λ.
check_reason: Several notes isolate intermediate unresolved steps, but scans27–28 provide the proof route. The cover and scan23 objectives are merged with that completed argument. The exact global/functorial scope remains limited by the later variance correction.

statement: The draft attempts the stronger statement that every endomorphism has square degree and determinant on the étale Tate module equal to its positive square root. Scan26 develops a canceled unrestricted sign character, and scan 27 retreats to positive Hermitian endomorphisms. A canceled polynomial-ring intersection assertion is also too strong.
reconstruction: Ordinary elliptic Frobenius has degree p, which need not be a square, and −1 has degree 1 but rank-one étale determinant −1. Zp∩Q is Z_(p), not Z. These counterexamples refute only the discarded general statements, not the live Rosati-positive argument.
check_reason: The notes’ proposed global sign obstruction is not retained as the author’s final position. Cancellation and the positive-Hermitian restriction are decisive.

statement: The determinant comparison is compatible with automorphisms only when the dual side uses the inverse dual action. For an isogeny u of an ordinary abelian variety, the two étale determinants for u and u* multiply to deg u; this does not make either determinant separately invariant under all morphisms.
reconstruction: The identity uses the dual multiplicative factor and the total p-divisible determinant, or the same algebraic degree polynomial after passage to rational endomorphisms. Read the automorphism statement with u*⁻¹, as written.
check_reason: The manuscript explicitly corrects the variance and limits its naturality. The earlier title’s canceled “fonctoriel” cannot be restored unrestrictedly.

statement: Remaining determinant questions are compatibility with dualizing A twice, direct sums/products, and reduction modulo p to the de Rham determinant comparison of scan22. The page leaves a sign question and a displayed final target without determinants.
reconstruction: Biduality and product normalizations can be formulated at the determinant-line level. The literal final full-module isomorphism cannot follow from a determinant isomorphism for g>1; missing det signs are a reading alarm, not an adopted correction.
check_reason: The note’s intended comparison is coherent for determinant lines, but the transcription’s rank mismatch and the unresolved biduality sign must remain visible.

statement: The auxiliary sheet8.4.4 predicts F-nilpotence above the middle degree and V-nilpotence below it, together with two middle-degree exact sequences involving crystalline torsion, coherent cohomology, and the free crystalline quotient. It expects the two sequences to be transposes under duality.
reconstruction: Here subscript ss means the bijective/stable Frobenius part of a finite-dimensional semilinear module, not a semisimple representation in the usual representation-theoretic sense. Superscript/subscript distinguish V and F. The claimed transpose relation is a self-flagged step; the scope of the earlier 8.1.2 assumptions must be carried.
check_reason: The notes correctly identify torsion terms but the degree conventions and dual stable operators are necessary. The auxiliary sequence is not read as a general degeneration theorem absent the preceding hypotheses.

statement: For X smooth proper over a perfect field k, W=W(k), derived reduction of crystalline cohomology gives de Rham cohomology, hence 0→H^i_cris(X)/p→H^i_dR(X)→H^(i+1)_cris(X)[p]→0. Comparing X and a smooth hypersurface Y gives the displayed snake-lemma kernel/cokernel sequence.
reconstruction: Derived base change, not naïve tensoring of individual cohomology groups, accounts for the shifted torsion term. The page attributes the theorem to Berthelot with an uncertain p≠2 restriction; modern statements include p=2 under the stated smooth-proper hypotheses.
check_reason: The exact sequence and its torsion index are present and survive the subsequent revisions. The attribution is recorded without upgrading the author’s uncertain historical scope.

statement: A route through crystalline Poincaré duality, Gysin maps and cup product with the polarization attempts to identify torsion correction terms in the vanishing-cohomology sequence. Its operative cup-product terms and accompanying explanation are canceled and the live sequence is altered.
reconstruction: The modern Poincaré/Gysin formalism is valid, but does not certify the canceled identification with the F-stable correction term. V/F duality and degree shifts must be retained. No vanished term is silently reintroduced from an earlier sheet.
check_reason: The notes correctly stress cancellation; the final sequence must be read from scans7–10 rather than reconstructed from the discarded w of8.5.3.

statement: The argument assumes an integral weak Lefschetz theorem: H^(n−1)_cris(X)→H^(n−1)_cris(Y) is injective with torsion-free cokernel, and the appropriate adjacent lower groups agree. It uses this to identify torsion restrictions and simplify the snake sequence.
reconstruction: Verified literature gives the integral statement for sufficiently high powers of an ample line bundle, with an explicit coherent-vanishing hypothesis; the pages speak of arbitrary smooth hyperplane sections of a chosen embedding. The stronger quantifier is not certified by that theorem.
check_reason: The required integral strength includes saturation, not just rational weak Lefschetz. The text later declares this an admitted ingredient, so it is a hypothesis of the displayed “Théorème”.

statement: For finite-dimensional k-vector spaces with p-semilinear endomorphism over a perfect field, the stable/bijective part is an exact functor. Unit-F modules correspond to finite-dimensional Fp-representations of the absolute Galois group, with compatible duals.
reconstruction: Use the Fitting decomposition into bijective and nilpotent summands. “Semisimple” here refers to the Frobenius operator’s stable part and does not assert semisimplicity of the Galois representation.
check_reason: The page explicitly introduces this translation; it underlies both the dimension formulas and the later relative local systems.

his_words: Ceci résulte aussitôt de la suite spectrale de Hodge
statement: The augmentation H^i_dR(X/k)→H^i(X,O_X) induces an isomorphism on Frobenius-stable parts. The argument uses Frobenius on the Hodge spectral sequence, zero on positive differential degree, and exactness of the stable-part functor.
reconstruction: For a clean finite-dimensional stable-part statement take k perfect and X proper with the de Rham complex under discussion. Smoothness makes the usual crystalline comparison available but is not needed for the formal Hodge-spectral-sequence argument. The margin refers to an auxiliary sheet, not an additional printed theorem.
check_reason: The page gives a genuine proof sketch. Its intermediate spectral-sequence reason is retained, not just the conclusion.

statement: Assuming the stated crystalline base-change, duality and integral weak-Lefschetz ingredients, the revised exact sequence is 0→ker v→H^n_cris(X)[p]_F,st→(E(Y)/p)_F,st→coker v→0, where v is restriction on stable H^(n−1)(O). Thus dim(E/p)_st=dim(coker v)+dim H^n[p]_st−dim ker v≥dim(coker v).
reconstruction: E is the crystalline cokernel and is free under the admitted integral Lefschetz hypothesis. The canceled cup-product w and end term are excluded. This is a conditional theorem, not an unconditional proof for all degrees.
check_reason: The formula is revised in the ink record. The notes that call the inequality an implication are correct, but the exact surviving torsion term and conditional status are essential.

statement: Over a finite field, the rank of the stable reduction of a free crystalline Frobenius module equals the number of slope-zero/unit eigenvalues. The page identifies these with corresponding ℓ-adic eigenvalues, conditional there on algebraicity of a Lefschetz operator, and distinguishes arithmetic Galois Frobenius from its inverse.
reconstruction: Use the q-linear Frobenius power, and count eigenvalues with multiplicity. The modern ℓ/crystalline characteristic-polynomial comparison removes that particular standard-conjecture proviso in the smooth-projective setting; it does not remove the integral hypothesis on E.
check_reason: The notes preserve the inverse-Frobenius correction and the manuscript’s explicit conditional comparison.

his_words: Je pense que l’homomorphisme v ... est injectif
statement: For X smooth projective connected of dimension n and Y a smooth hypersurface section, restriction H^(n−1)(X,O)_F,st→H^(n−1)(Y,O)_F,st is expected injective. The page states it for n=2, and for degrees d with H^(n−1)(X,O_X(−d))=0.
reconstruction: The vanishing condition proves the latter case through the coherent long exact sequence. The surface case is accessible through étale H¹ and Lefschetz π₁. The all-dimensional/all-degree claim requires a separate theorem.
check_reason: The note accurately retains both proved cases and the general “je pense”; these quantifiers are not merged.

statement: On a suitable open set of smooth degree-d hypersurface sections where the stable coherent rank is maximal, the unit-F pieces should form finite Fp-local systems and the revised sequence should vary relatively. Its kernel comes from the base-field crystalline torsion. Over a finite field a finite scalar extension makes the base-field Frobenius action trivial, reducing mod-p eigenvalue variation to the Hasse–Witt representation.
reconstruction: Shrink enough to obtain finite locally free stable modules and constant ranks. Over an imperfect base use a relative unit map F*E≃E, not an invertible semilinear map on the same coefficients. Constant rank of the crystalline term also requires control of ker v; the high-degree case supplies it.
check_reason: The earlier notes correctly identify the local-system programme, but maximum coherent stable rank alone is not every base-change and kernel hypothesis. The page itself retains the ker v qualification.

his_words: Or cela est établi au n°7
statement: For generic smooth degree-d hypersurface sections and all sufficiently large d, the stable vanishing coherent cohomology should have positive dimension, yielding a p-adic unit eigenvalue in critical vanishing cohomology. The author suggests equivalence with maximal motivic level n−1 and refers to a result in an absent section7.
reconstruction: The positivity/growth question has a precise Hasse–Witt formulation. The exact motivic-level equivalence cannot be identified without the missing definition and section7; no broad standard-conjecture statement is substituted.
check_reason: The manuscript’s margin claims an earlier internal result, but that result is not present in the supplied cote 4 pages. The exact positivity assertion is later proved in SGA7II, XXI, Theorem 1.4 for projective equidimensional Cohen–Macaulay X and all sufficiently large d. Its motivic equivalence remains a separate question.

statement: If X with polarization lifts to characteristic 0, the author hopes to express the torsion sufficient condition for bijectivity of φ through p-adic étale cohomology of a characteristic-zero lift.
reconstruction: Modern integral p-adic comparison gives a one-sided torsion-length inequality and strict examples, so a blanket identification of crystalline and étale torsion is false. That does not by itself decide an equivalence for the exact stable-part condition used here.
check_reason: The page asks for a future comparison and does not claim a proven integral comparison theorem. Its canceled attempt to remove ss indices is not adopted.

statement: The earlier draft seeks failure of surjectivity and proposes higher-dimensional products. The amended sequence always makes φ surjective, so the surviving request is nonbijectivity/noninjectivity. The projective-space product construction is canceled.
reconstruction: The canceled product also overlooks that positive-degree crystalline cohomology of projective space has positive Frobenius slope, hence zero F-stable reduction. It is retained as a discarded experiment only.
check_reason: Entries136 and141 cannot remain live conjectures about nonsurjectivity after the exact-sequence correction. The product programme is not a validated general example.

his_words: L’exemple de Serre au symposium de Mexico
statement: The revised criterion says φ is bijective iff ker v→H^n_cris(X)[p]_st is onto; when v is injective this is equivalent to H^n[p]_st=0. A free Z/p quotient of a suitable complete intersection supplies a smooth surface with H¹_cris=0 and H¹_et(Fp)=Fp, hence nonzero stable p-torsion in H²_cris and noninjective φ.
reconstruction: The further assertion that φ-bijectivity is equivalent in general to equality between dim H^(n−1)(O)_st and the free crystalline stable rank also involves the preceding torsion H^(n−1)_cris/p. It is valid in the surface example where H¹_cris is torsion-free, but requires qualification in higher dimension.
check_reason: The notes correctly isolate the Serre example and the new torsion correction; they do not expose the extra term in the general equality criterion.

statement: For n≥2 and the generic maximal-rank locus of degree-d hypersurface sections of a fixed smooth projective X, ask whether the nonconstant stable coherent vanishing local system is irreducible, or even has image GL_r(Fp). The text excludes a trivial n=1 projective-line case.
reconstruction: Geometric and arithmetic monodromy must be distinguished. A full GL_r(Fp) result for a special universal curve family, or an ℓ-adic Lefschetz result, does not answer this all-X unit-Frobenius question.
check_reason: The question and its stronger full-image variant are explicit. No exact theorem for these quantifiers is supplied by the notes.

his_words: tout élément de Fp est trace
statement: Assuming full GL_r(Fp) monodromy and r≥2, every residue occurs as a matrix trace. Together with the Woods Hole congruence and Chebotarev, the author expects every prescribed residue modulo p for #Y(k′), with Y in any given nonempty open of the degree-d parameter space and k′/k some finite extension. He also expects r to tend to infinity with d.
reconstruction: The finite extension varies. Trace surjectivity is elementary for r≥2; the arithmetic conclusion needs control of the constant cohomology contributions and the Frobenius coset. The rank-growth input is established by Koblitz’s Theorem 1 and Lemma 4. The page’s historical statement that the congruences are not known, even for plane curves, is not a present-day status claim.
check_reason: The notes correctly separate the elementary conditional implication from the monodromy and rank-growth inputs. Later literature settles rank growth; the fixed-X full-monodromy formulation is not verified. The finite-field/open-set quantifiers are retained.
